title: Depend on the git-diff-parser library for GitDiffKit (step 1.4)
body:
Step 1.4 of the split plan, with step 1.5's checks as its end-to-end tests: swift-steward now takes `GitDiffKit` from [marosoaie/git-diff-parser](https://github.com/marosoaie/git-diff-parser) instead of carrying its own copy.

## What changed

- **Dependency.** `Sources/GitDiffKit` and the `GitDiffKit` product are gone. `Package.swift` depends on `https://github.com/marosoaie/git-diff-parser.git` `from: "0.1.0"` (a tag only, never a branch or a revision), and `Package.resolved` pins `0.1.0` at `ce8bbbf`. `DiffDiagnostics`, the CLI and the tests use `.product(name: "GitDiffKit", package: "git-diff-parser")`. `StreamParsing` stays an internal target here (decision 2).
- **Package `name` is now `swift-steward` (a deviation from the brief, which said to leave it for 1.6).** It has to change. SwiftPM matches root packages to dependencies by manifest name, so a root named `git-diff-parser` is taken as an override of the dependency. Resolution then fails:
  `error: unable to override package 'git-diff-parser' because its identity 'git-diff-parser' doesn't match override's identity (directory name) 'step-1-4-depend-on-library-b8991c'`.
  Only the `name:` changes. It is not the package identity, which comes from the URL and is already `swift-steward` for consumers (the README has always used `package: "swift-steward"`). The executable product, the `git-diff-parser` binary and the formula are untouched and stay for 1.6. The one visible effect is the derived Xcode scheme: `git-diff-parser-Package` → `swift-steward-Package` (AGENTS.md updated). `release.yml` and the formula don't use the scheme.
- **Checkout-directory trap (documented in AGENTS.md).** A root package's identity is its directory name, so a checkout in a directory named exactly `git-diff-parser` also shadows the dependency: `product 'GitDiffKit' required by package 'git-diff-parser' target 'git-diff-parser' not found`. Fresh clones in `swift-steward/` (as in CI) and in a brew-style staging directory (`git-diff-parser-<date>-<pid>-<random>`, `swift build -c release --disable-sandbox`, as in the formula) both build.
- **Tests.** The target is renamed `GitDiffKitTests` → `SwiftStewardTests` and keeps the tests for BuildLogKit, DiffDiagnostics, StreamParsing and the CLI. 36 GitDiffKit tests are deleted. Each one has an **identical** copy in the library at `0.1.0`, checked by diffing against `git show 0.1.0:Tests/GitDiffKitTests/…`, so no test was dropped without an equivalent:
  - `DiffParserTests`: all 16.
  - `MalformedInputTests`: the 7 diff regressions. The clang `fatal error:` test stays.
  - `LineRangeSetTests` (6) and the 4 diff-only `Streaming` tests (whole string, chunked equivalence, unterminated last line, CRLF), plus the diff half of the over-long-line test. Its log half and the log chunking test stay.
  - `RealDiffTests`: the PR #70000 totals/spot checks and the chunking test. Both CLI end-to-end tests stay.
  - `RealWorldDiffTests`: the kernel totals test.
- **The numstat oracle now runs through the CLI.** It takes the `changes` JSON per-file counts and checks them against `git apply --numstat` on all three real-world fixtures, so the end-to-end path keeps an independent oracle here. The oracle now passes `-z`, which prints paths raw. The old version borrowed the parser's own (now inaccessible, internal) `DiffParser.unquote`, so the oracle shared code with what it checked. On the three fixtures, `-z` yields the same records (13,479 / 1,133 / 161, none quoted).
- **New test: CRLF build logs.** StreamParsing's CR stripping used to be reached only by the diff parser's CRLF test, which moved to the library. The new test feeds a CRLF log both whole and in 1-byte chunks, so each CR and its LF land in different chunks. Disabling the CR strip makes it fail; with the strip in place it passes.
- **Docs.** AGENTS.md (the product table, the tag-only rule, `swift package edit` for lockstep work, the name/directory trap, the scheme), README (the library snippet takes GitDiffKit from git-diff-parser) and INTERNALS.md (points to the library's notes, says which tests live where).

## Tests run

All on Xcode 26.2 / Swift 6.2.3, macOS 26 (Apple Silicon).

| Command | Inputs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `swift build --build-tests` | – | Build complete, 0 warnings |
| `swift test` (network tests on) | cached kernel, redis and swift-argument-parser fixtures | **34 tests in 8 suites passed** (~18 s) |
| `GIT_DIFF_PARSER_SKIP_NETWORK_TESTS=1 swift test` | – | 34 tests in 8 suites passed, real-world suite skipped (1 s) |
| `xcodebuild test -scheme swift-steward-Package -destination platform=macOS` | – | **TEST SUCCEEDED**, 34 tests in 8 suites; no compiler warnings |
| `swiftlint lint --quiet` | whole tree | prints nothing |
| `swift test` on the first commit (old tests, unchanged, against the library) | – | 69 tests in 10 suites passed |
| CRLF test mutation check (CR strip disabled) | – | fails with 2 issues; passes with the strip restored |
| fresh `git clone` + `swift build` | dirs `swift-steward/`, `git-diff-parser-20261023-4242-1abcdef/` (release, `--disable-sandbox`), `git-diff-parser/` | build, build, **fails** (expected, documented) |
| `swift test --enable-code-coverage` | – | Sources/ line coverage **95.10%** (369/388); main: 94.22% (734/779) |

### End to end: outputs byte-identical (step 1.5)

Three release binaries, each run on the same inputs. For every case, stdout, stderr and the exit code are compared with `cmp`:
- `v1.0.2`: `/opt/homebrew/bin/git-diff-parser` from brew.
- `main`: built from `main` @ `fb73407`, before this change.
- `new`: built from this branch.

Inputs:
- **Diffs:** Linux 6.6→6.7 (70 MB), redis 7.0.0→7.2.0, swift-argument-parser 1.0.0→1.5.0, and the swift PR #70000 fixture.
- **Real logs from swift-argument-parser 1.5.0:**
  - `xcodebuild build`: 18 warnings.
  - `swift build`: 0 warnings.
  - `swiftlint lint`: 2,127 warnings, 349 errors.
  - `swiftformat --lint`: 25,643 diagnostics.
- **Real log from redis 7.2.0:** `clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra src/*.c`, with 1,003 warnings.
- **Sonar JSON:**
  - The unit-test report, against a matching diff.
  - A 2,476-issue `issues/search` report built from the real SwiftLint violations. It mixes in every shape the parser handles: legacy severities, impacts-only issues, textRange-only issues, resolved issues and file-level issues.

44 cases:
- `changes` json/text on all 4 diffs, plus 2 stdin runs.
- `filter` with `--tool` xcodebuild/generic/swiftlint/swiftformat/sonar × `--format` json/github/text, plus `--repo-root`, `--tolerance`, `--fail-on` (exit 1) and stdin for the log or the diff.

| Comparison | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` vs `new` | **132/132 files identical** (44 cases × stdout/stderr/exit) |
| `v1.0.2` vs `new` | **111/111 identical** on the 37 cases v1.0.2 supports; the 7 Sonar cases have no v1.0.2 counterpart (`--tool sonar` landed in #15, after v1.0.2) |
| `v1.0.2` vs `main` | 111/111 identical (baseline sanity) |

### Benchmark (release builds, `/usr/bin/time -l`)

| Case | v1.0.2 | main | new |
|---|---|---|---|
| `changes` kernel 6.6→6.7 (70 MB), 5 runs, median | 0.19 s, 68 MB | 0.18 s, 67 MB | **0.17 s, 67 MB** |
| `changes -` 6× kernel via stdin (422 MB), 3 runs, median | 0.80 s, 68 MB | 0.74 s, 67 MB | **0.64 s, 67 MB** |
| `filter` swiftformat log (25,643 diagnostics) vs kernel diff, 3 runs | 1.14 s, 43 MB | 1.12 s, 43 MB | **1.12 s, 43 MB** |

The new build is within the ~0.2 s / 70 MB budget and its peak memory is flat.

### Coverage

The ruleset requires at least 70% coverage and allows at most a 1-point drop. Sources/ line coverage from `swift test --enable-code-coverage` (llvm-cov export, first-party `Sources/` only):

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Sources/ line coverage | 94.22% (734/779) | **95.10% (369/388)** |

The CLI runs as a subprocess, so it isn't counted in either number. Before the CRLF test was added, the number was 94.07%.

## Review

`codex review --base main` (model `gpt-6.1-sol`, stdin closed) on `a2443b2`: **0 findings**. It reported "No actionable regressions found; the pinned GitDiffKit dependency preserves the removed implementation's behavior." Its sandbox kept it from running the Swift tests; the suites above were run outside it. Nothing to fix.
